C0.quote: draw a broad picture on the subgame perfect implementability of voting rules
C0.note: Studies which voting rules (social choice rules: scoring rules, runoff, Condorcet consistent, compromise rules) are implementable in subgame perfect equilibrium; strategic aspects of voting procedures.

C1.quote: establishing a nuanced picture over the subgame perfect implementability of compromise rules
C1.note: Main results show which rules satisfy or violate Condition alpha/beta (properties of rules), which by Abreu-Sen characterise implementability via subgame perfect equilibria of extensive form mechanisms (EQ). No equilibrium is computed directly; most results are property checks, hence AX primary.

C2.2.quote: transitive and antisymmetric binary relations on X
C2.2.note: Linear orders. Condorcet consistent rules in Section 4 use the majority relation derived from the profile, but the rule's argument remains the profile.

C2.3.quote: is endowed with a preference relation P i ∈ P
C2.3.note: Agents are endowed with preferences; the SCR is defined on the profile of these preferences.

C2.4.loc: 2 Basic notions and notation, p.4; footnote 1, p.1; footnotes 10-11, pp.7-8
C2.4.quote: is endowed with a preference relation P i ∈ P
C2.4.note: The SCR is a function of the endowed preference profile. Implementation via a mechanism (footnote 1) implicitly separates mechanism play from preferences, but the mechanism and its messages are never defined. Footnotes 10-11 say voters 'announce'/'submit' a ranking under runoff/STV without relating it to held preferences; DIST was considered but no separate notation or statement that submissions may differ is given.

C3.1.quote: the set of subgame perfect equilibrium outcomes of Γ coincides with
C3.1.note: Every main result concerns subgame perfect implementability, i.e. strategic play by agents in an extensive form mechanism whose equilibrium outcomes must equal f at the true profile. Agents' messages in the mechanism are not modelled explicitly in the paper; results are obtained by checking Condition alpha/beta.

C4.1.note: Input is RANK, but no utility, welfare, satisfaction, cost, distortion or intensity notion is used; 'Welfare' appears only in journal names/reference titles.

C4.2.note: 'Dichotomous preferences' not used; 'Borda-Condorcet dichotomy' refers to rule families, not preferences.

C5.1.quote: no Pareto optimal social choice rule is Maskin monotonic
C5.1.note: Marginal: the only efficiency-related statement is a cited result (Asan and Sanver 2006) in a footnote; the paper's own results make no welfare, efficiency, representation or distortion claims.

C5.2.quote: no Pareto optimal social choice rule is Maskin monotonic
C5.2.note: Pareto optimality is relative to the individual preferences in the profile, which are the rule's argument (C2.4 = IDU); no statement relating input to held attitudes.

VOT.quote_behav: for a social choice rule to be implementable via subgame perfect equilibria
VOT.loc_info: Checked: Abstract; 1 Introduction; 2 Basic notions and notation; 3-5; 6 Final remarks; Appendix A
VOT.note: Agents' strategic behaviour is stated only by naming the solution concept (subgame perfect equilibrium of a mechanism); no explicit description of optimisation. What agents know about others' preferences is never stated (complete information, standard in this literature, is not mentioned; 'information sets' appears only for Dutta-Sen game trees).

DES.note: Mechanisms are mentioned (existence of a mechanism Γ, canonical mechanism of Abreu-Sen) but no designer's choice or objective is modelled.
